title: The Vermont Health Data Sovereignty Initiative: A 2026 Technical Roadmap
summary: As the CTO for the Vermont Agency of Digital Services, I present this technical roadmap for establishing data sovereignty within the VHIE. This report outlines the shift from passive document repositories to active liquidity fabrics and the economic deflationary dividends expected by 2030.

children.text: In my capacity as CTO for the State of Vermont, I have observed that our primary obstacle to health transformation is not a lack of data, but the inherent friction within our legacy infrastructure. We are moving toward a 'Sovereignty' model where clinical identity is portable, secure, and governed by the patient rather than the vendor.
KEY STRATEGIC GOAL: Achieve a 40% reduction in technical debt by transitioning 85% of rural critical access hospitals to the unified VHIE Liquidity Fabric by Q4 2027.

children.text: The architecture above represents our transition toward a FHIR-native ecosystem. By decoupling the data layer from the application layer, we enable what I call 'Technical Deflation'—the lowering of maintenance costs through standardized API protocols.
III. The Executive Insight: Policy vs. Execution

body.title: CTO Briefing: The Interoperability Fabric
body.summary: An 12-minute technical breakdown of how Vermont is overcoming policy friction to enable real-time data liquidity across state lines.

children.text: We do not seek to build a bigger database; we seek to build a more liquid network. In the digital age, a static record is a dead record.
IV. Scalability and the Future of Value-Based Care

children.text: The road ahead requires a relentless focus on data integrity. Our Agency of Human Services (AHS) partners are already seeing the benefits of this liquidity through reduced administrative overhead and improved clinical outcomes in rural districts. We will continue to scale this fabric until every Vermonter has full sovereignty over their digital health footprint.
